description: Table 3 is a rendered-image table (no axes, no plot panels, no micrograph) headed "Range" and "Sensitivity", containing two data rows: "Force" and "Displacement". The Force row gives a Range of "1–10 mN" and a Sensitivity of "100 nN"; the Displacement row gives a Range of "5 μm" and a Sensitivity of "0.2 nm". These are the only cells present — there are no footnotes, additional columns or numeric entries — and all values are printed verbatim in the image. The group is a single unlabelled panel: there are no (a)/(b) sub-figures and no curves, spectra, maps or photographs to read. Its role is instrumental rather than scientific. The citing sentence states that a nano-indentation instrument (Triboscope, Hysitron Inc.) is set onto an AFM stage (SPM-9500J2, Shimazdu Co.) and that Table 3 presents the specification of that equipment. The table therefore documents the measurement capability behind the paper's microscopic elastic-modulus measurements — force read over a 1–10 mN range with 100 nN sensitivity, displacement over a 5 μm range with 0.2 nm sensitivity — rather than demonstrating any material result, and it fixes the resolution limits within which nano-indentation data elsewhere in the paper were acquired. No sample, alloy or processing condition appears.

The 'Force' row reports a Sensitivity of '100 nN'.
The 'Displacement' row reports a Range of '5 μm'.
The 'Displacement' row reports a Sensitivity of '0.2 nm'.
The table has exactly two column headers, 'Range' and 'Sensitivity', and no further columns or footnotes.
The table contains no sample label, alloy composition or processing condition — it characterises the indentation equipment only.
The caption identifies the table as 'Specification of the nano-indentation equipment'.
The citing text states that a nano-indentation instrument (Triboscope, Hysitron Inc.) is set onto an AFM stage (SPM-9500J2, Shimazdu Co.), which the table's specifications describe.
